name: Question 3
problem:
Complete the arguments in the reasoning below to find the Laplace transform of $f(t)={e}^{7t}.$First, we apply the definition of the Laplace transform:

$$
L{f(t)}=F(s)={{field-1}}
$$

We now examine the convergence of $F(s)$ for different values of $s:$

$\,$ For {{field-2}}
the integral is divergent.

$\,$ For {{field-3}}
the integral is convergent.

Evaluating our integral in the convergent case, we have

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{(7-s)t}\,\text{d}t={{field-4}}.
$$

∫0∞e(7−s)tdt
∫0∞e(7−s)tdt
∫−∞∞e(7−s)tdt
∫−∞∞e(7+s)tdt
∫0∞e(7+s)tdt
L{f(t)}=F(s)={(∫−∞∞e(7−s)tdt)(S0)}

We now examine the convergence of F(s) for different values of s:

For
s≤7
s>7
s≤7
the integral is divergent.

For
s>7
s>7
s≤7
s≥7
the integral is convergent.

Evaluating our integral in the convergent case, we have

 
1s−7
